title: Nonstop US-Okinawa Flights to Start in 2027
paragraphs: With its beautiful beaches, warm weather and unique culture, Okinawa is a popular travel destination for many Japanese people — as well as people from nearby places like Taiwan, South Korea and Hong Kong.
However, it's a little harder for people from the mainland US to get to Okinawa ㅊthey usually have to travel through Tokyo first, or even through Taiwan or Hong Kong.
But that will change next year.
United Airlines will start nonstop flights between San Francisco and Naha, Okinawa, on March 27, 2027.
The new route will be Okinawa's only scheduled nonstop service to the US mainland.
The new flights will run three times a week. Flying from San Francisco to Naha will take about 13 hours and 15 minutes. The trip back will take around 11 hours.
At the moment, Naha Airport's longest international route is to Singapore, which takes about five hours.
The San Francisco flights will be available between late March and late October — with the average temperature in Naha still being 25 degrees Celsius in October!

Okinawa has a long history with the US. After World War II, the islands were under US control for 27 years, and were only returned to Japanese control in 1972. The islands are still home to more than 30 US bases, with over 20,000 troops in Kadena Air Base just 20 kilometers northeast of Naha.

The new Okinawa flight is just one of 10 new flights United announced. The airline is also adding daily nonstop flights between Los Angeles and Osaka, as well as flights to places in Europe like Luxembourg, Toulouse and Ibiza.
